workedExamples.prompt: State the source-locked fact for “kinetic-energy unit”.

commonMistakes: Square the speed, not the mass.
Convert mass to kilograms before substitution.
Do not treat doubling speed as simply doubling kinetic energy.
A partly correct response can still miss a required unit, relationship, control variable or explanation link.
detailedExplanation: Verified against The Tiffin Girls’ School Year 9 Physics Curriculum Outline 2026–27 and aligned to AQA GCSE Physics 8463.
The kinetic energy of a moving object is given by Eₖ = ½mv², where m is mass in kilograms and v is speed in metres per second.
Kinetic energy is proportional to mass but proportional to the square of speed. Doubling the mass doubles kinetic energy; doubling the speed makes kinetic energy four times as large.
Because speed is squared, errors in speed measurement can have a large effect on a calculated kinetic energy.
When an object speeds up, energy is transferred into its kinetic store. When it slows down, energy is transferred out of that store to other stores.
examTips: Write Eₖ = ½mv² and calculate v² before multiplying by mass.
